body.statement:
Under the observed-law conditions and the simultaneous conditional-parallel-trends condition on the baseline-treatment support \(X_0\), the bounded-slope/Lipschitz completion class \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever these sets are nonempty,
\[
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}=\Theta(P).
\]
For every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), the affine one-argument static-schedule lift produces \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), preserves the entire joint law \(P\), satisfies \(m_{Q_u}=u\in C(X_0)\), and makes both period schedules individually \(K\)-Lipschitz. Moreover, on one common full-probability event,
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)\qquad\text{for every }d\in I,
\]
so the lift satisfies the stronger all-\(I\) parallel-trends equality and \(\theta(Q_u)=\{T-J_P(u)\}/A\). This theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its model is not the class defined by Assumptions 1--4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024): the theorem additionally imposes the finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, continuity of the observed regression version \(g\), and the simultaneous diagonal clause in parallel trends. Thus no equality or global inclusion of the two observed-law models is asserted. On an observed law that satisfies the published assumptions, \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is only the restricted slice satisfying these extra conditions, and \(\Theta(P)\) is not asserted to be the published-class identified set. The result is a sharp bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity repair after failure of the published singleton claim, not a sharp characterization of the unrestricted published class.
body.proof_tex:
Compactness of \(I\) and the support condition give \(|Z|\leq\operatorname{diam}(I)\) almost surely. The no-stayer condition gives \(|Z|>0\) almost surely. Consequently
\[
0<A=E_P|Z|\leq\operatorname{diam}(I)<\infty.
\]
Observed integrability implies \(E_P|\Delta Y|<\infty\), and hence \(T=E_P[S\Delta Y]\) is finite because \(|S|=1\) almost surely.

Take \(Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\) and put \(m=m_Q\). Consistency gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta Y
&=Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\\
&=\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}
  +\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The simultaneous clause in conditional parallel trends provides one \(Q\)-full event on which its conditional-mean equality holds for every \(d\in X_0\). Since \(D_1=X\in X_0\) almost surely, evaluation on the diagonal \(d=X\) is therefore legitimate and yields
\[
E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z\right]=m(X).
\]
Taking the conditional expectation of the preceding decomposition, using the observed-law match and the declared support version of \(g\), gives
\[
g(x,z)-m(x)
=E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\mid X=x,Z=z\right]
\]
for \(P_{XZ}\)-almost every \((x,z)\). The conditional mean-movement bound therefore implies
\[
|g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|
\qquad P_{XZ}\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]
The function \((x,z)\mapsto |g(x,z)-m(x)|-K|z|\) is continuous on \(H\): continuity of \(g\) is assumed and \(m\in C(X_0)\) is part of the legal-completion definition. If it were positive at any point of \(H=\operatorname{supp}_P(X,Z)\), it would remain positive on a relatively open neighborhood having positive \(P_{XZ}\)-probability, contradicting the almost-everywhere inequality. Hence
\[
|g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|\qquad\text{for every }(x,z)\in H.
\]
Together with the trend bound and the global Lipschitz condition in \(\mathfrak Q(P)\), this proves \(m\in\mathcal C_P\), and hence
\[
\mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing.
\]

The same decomposition identifies the causal functional without defining it to equal an observed functional. By iterated expectations, the diagonal equality above, and the definition of the signed measure \(\nu_P\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
A\theta(Q)
&=E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
&=E_P[S\Delta Y]
  -E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
&=T-E_P[S m(X)]\\
&=T-\int_{X_0}m(x)\,d\nu_P(x)
=T-J_P(m).
\end{aligned}
\]
The integrals are finite because \(m\) is bounded. Thus every value generated by \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) belongs to \(\Theta(P)\).

Conversely, fix \(u\in\mathcal C_P\) and retain the observed vector with law \(P\). On \(\{Z\neq0\}\), define
\[
b_u=\frac{g(X,Z)-u(X)}{Z},
\]
and put \(b_u=0\) on the \(P\)-null event \(\{Z=0\}\). Measurability follows from the continuity, hence Borel measurability, of \(g\) and \(u\) on their supports. The support inequalities defining \(\mathcal C_P\) give
\[
|b_u|\leq K\qquad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Define simultaneously for all \(d\in I\)
\[
Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=Y_1+b_u(d-D_1),
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)=Y_2+b_u(d-D_2).
\]
These are jointly measurable static schedules. They satisfy consistency pointwise:
\[
Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)=Y_2.
\]
Therefore the entire joint observed law remains \(P\), not merely a collection of its moments. For every fixed \(d\in I\), compactness of \(I\), the bound on \(b_u\), and observed integrability give
\[
|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|\leq |Y_t|+K\operatorname{diam}(I),
\qquad
E_{Q_u}|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|<\infty.
\]
For every \(d,d'\in I\),
\[
|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)-Y_t^{Q_u}(d')|
=|b_u|\,|d-d'|
\leq K|d-d'|,
\]
so both schedules are individually \(K\)-Lipschitz.

Their period difference does not depend on the dose argument:
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)
&=\Delta Y+b_u(D_1-D_2)\\
&=\Delta Y-b_uZ\\
&=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)
\end{aligned}
\]
for every \(d\in I\), on one common event. Since \(g(X,Z)=E_P[\Delta Y\mid X,Z]\), this identity implies, simultaneously for every \(d\in I\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X,Z]
&=u(X),\\
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X]
&=u(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the strengthened all-\(I\) parallel-trends equality holds, including its diagonal clause, and the displayed version gives \(m_{Q_u}=u\) on \(X_0\). The bound and Lipschitz restrictions on \(m_{Q_u}\) follow from \(u\in\mathcal C_P\). Moreover,
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)
=b_uZ
=g(X,Z)-u(X),
\]
and therefore
\[
\left|E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)\mid X,Z]\right|
\leq K|Z|.
\]
All defining conditions of \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) are now verified, so \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\). This proves the reverse nonemptiness implication. Finally,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta(Q_u)
&=\frac{E_P[S\{g(X,Z)-u(X)\}]}{A}\\
&=\frac{T-J_P(u)}{A},
\end{aligned}
\]
because iterated expectations give \(E_P[Sg(X,Z)]=E_P[S\Delta Y]=T\). Every point of \(\Theta(P)\) is therefore attained by a legal full-data law, while the first half of the proof excludes every other value.

The assumptions used in this argument are exactly the displayed dependencies: marginal quasi-stayers never enter. The finite movement bound, bounded globally Lipschitz trend, continuous support version, and simultaneous diagonal clause are additional restrictions relative to the published model. Consequently the proved set equality is confined to \(\mathfrak Q(P)\); it cannot be transferred to a larger completion class merely because both classes satisfy the source's basic causal restrictions.
body.justification: This is the causal kernel: it replaces an unsupported conditional limit by a two-sided, full-observed-law sharp characterization.
body.gap: Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) imposes only \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta)>0\), while the Appendix proof of Theorem 1 invokes \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta\mid D_1)>0\) immediately before display (4). Under the source's parallel-trends condition on the baseline-treatment support, the present theorem gives a sharp sensitivity-class characterization after failure of the published singleton claim. Assumption 5 of de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1) supplies an analogous baseline-conditional support regime, but its Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
body.consumer: Applied continuous-dose DiD analyses with changing temperatures can report a robustness set without imposing a parametric extrapolation across baseline-specific support holes.
